ULTA.thesis_one_line: Largest US beauty specialty retailer, comps re-accelerating and guidance raised twice this year, but Sephora's expansion inside Kohl's is a real structural share threat.
kill_criteria: Comparable sales growth below 2.0% for two consecutive quarters (below the low end of the raised FY26 guide range).
FY26 diluted EPS guidance cut from the current $28.70-29.00 range at any subsequent quarterly release.
Gross margin below 38.5% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 39.1-40.1% in the last four quarters shown above).
Net new Sephora-at-Kohl's door count growth re-accelerates materially (company/press disclosure) alongside a renewed comp deceleration below 3%, confirming share loss rather than a temporary lapse.
Short-term debt balance grows beyond $500M while cash stays below $200M, signalling buybacks are being funded by leverage rather than FCF.
key_adverse_facts: Comp sales growth decelerated sequentially within FY26 from +5.3% (Q1) to +3.8% (Q2), and Sephora inside Kohl's has expanded past 1,100 doors with an estimated >$2bn annual sales run-rate, a structural not cyclical share-donor dynamic.
12-month price momentum is negative (-1.8% per b1 factor data) despite the earnings beats.

Cash fell to $158.5M (from $424.2M at FY25-end) and short-term debt rose to $339.6M, partly to fund an accelerated $1.8bn FY26 buyback plan; EPS growth (+13-16%) is running well ahead of operating-income growth (+10-12%), meaning a meaningful share of the beat is capital allocation, not organic execution.
No SBC disclosure, insider Form 4 review, or risk-factor diff vs prior-year 10-K was completed this pass (time-box limitation).
data_conflicts: None material this pass; b1 quant snapshot (last_filed_date 2026-08-27) is current with the dossier's primary period.
ULTA.confidence_in_thesis: medium - comp reacceleration is only one quarter old and negative price momentum suggests the market has not yet endorsed the durability of the improvement

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists yet for ULTA (wave 6 not yet valued by the systematic model), so v1_verdict is null and there is nothing to reconcile; my own reverse-DCF sense (FCF yield ~4.6%, WACC ~8.5%) implies ~4-5% perpetual FCF/EPS growth, at or slightly below my base case of 5-7%, i.e. fairly priced with modest upside if the comp reacceleration holds.

ULTA.scenario_basis: Starting point FY26 guided diluted EPS ~$28.85 (midpoint); base case assumes 5-7% EPS/FCF growth (3-4% comps + margin/mix + buyback accretion) with exit P/E ~18x (roughly in line with current 18.9x NTM); bear assumes comp growth stalls near 0-1% with margin pressure from Sephora competition and exit multiple compresses to ~14x; bull assumes comps sustain 5%+ as Space NK and loyalty relaunch work, exit multiple re-rates to ~22x; no meaningful dividend (buybacks are the return-of-capital vehicle, embedded in per-share growth, not added separately).

VMC.thesis_one_line: Largest US construction-aggregates producer using pricing power and record cash margins to offset soft private-construction volumes, with a strong, under-levered balance sheet.
kill_criteria: Aggregates segment shipment growth negative (a decline in tons shipped YoY) for two consecutive quarters.
Total debt / TTM Adjusted EBITDA rises above the top of management's own stated target range, 2.5x (from 1.9x as of 2026-06-30).
FY26 Adjusted EBITDA guidance cut below the current $2.4-2.6bn range at any subsequent quarterly release.
Freight-adjusted mix-adjusted aggregates pricing growth falls below 2% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +5% in Q2 FY26).
Cash gross profit per ton declines YoY for two consecutive quarters (from the current record $12.02/ton).
key_adverse_facts: Aggregates shipment growth was only +1% YoY in Q2 FY26 (with Texas/Southeast volumes hit by weather); growth remains entirely price-led, not volume-led, and the 28.9x trailing GAAP P/E leaves limited room for volume disappointment.
12-month price momentum is sharply negative (-11.7% per b1 factor data).

The eight-year NAFTA arbitration against Mexico concluded in July 2026 with the tribunal finding Mexico in violation but awarding only 'negligible' monetary damages - a legacy legal exposure that did not pay off as hoped.

VMC.scenario_basis: Starting point TTM diluted EPS $8.49 (GAAP, cont. ops) and TTM Adjusted EBITDA $2,354M; base case assumes 5-6% EPS/FCF growth (2-4% pricing above cost inflation + bolt-on M&A) with exit P/E ~24x (below current 28.9x, reflecting some multiple normalization); bear assumes volumes decline further and pricing growth fades to 1-2%, exit multiple compresses to ~19x; bull assumes public/infrastructure-driven volume recovery plus continued 4-5% pricing, exit multiple holds near 27x; modest dividend yield (~0.6-0.8%) added in all scenarios.

APO.thesis_one_line: Alternative-asset manager plus Athene annuities platform growing AUM and fee earnings 25% a year and trading cheap on core earnings, but a June 2026 private-credit fund gating event confirms real liquidity stress in its wealth-channel products.
kill_criteria: A second fund-gating or redemption-cap event at Apollo (any vehicle) disclosed within the next four quarters, or aggregate redemption requests exceeding 20% of NAV in any Apollo semi-liquid vehicle.
Fee Related Earnings growth turns negative YoY in any quarter (from +25% YoY in Q2 2026).
A GAAP net loss in any quarter not attributable to a clearly disclosed one-time item (i.e., a loss driven by core operating or credit losses rather than a tax/accounting adjustment).

Any public disclosure of a downgrade to Athene's financial-strength ratings, or realized (not just mark-to-market) credit losses on Athene's invested-asset portfolio exceeding a materially adverse threshold disclosed in a future filing.
Total AUM growth decelerates below 10% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +25% YoY in Q2 2026).
key_adverse_facts: Confirmed private-credit fund gating in June 2026 after redemption requests reached approximately 17% of NAV (offshore investors ~12.5%, US onshore ~4.3%); Apollo's own disclosure put expected ADS net outflows at roughly $400M YTD, ~3% of NAV, for Q2 2026 - a real, dated, company-specific liquidity-stress event, not just industry-wide press speculation.

Q1 2026 GAAP net loss of $(1,930)M / $(3.27) diluted EPS, driven by a one-time $1.7bn Bermuda deferred-tax valuation-allowance charge disclosed in the company's own filing; trailing GAAP EPS/P/E is therefore unreliable for valuation purposes.

GAAP net income is highly volatile from quarter to quarter due to insurance-portfolio investment mark-to-market swings (Investment related gains (losses) moved from $(2,078)M in Q1 2026 to +$2,989M in Q2 2026), a structural feature of the Athene-linked balance sheet, not an operating trend.

The pre-registered quant factor model ranks APO in the bottom decile (decile 1) on its composite score, driven by GAAP-based ROE/earnings-yield metrics; this dossier attributes most of that to GAAP noise but flags it as a signal worth respecting rather than fully explaining away.
FCF yield and EBIT/EV factors are not available (NaN) in the b1 dataset for this name, a genuine data gap for an insurance/asset-manager hybrid.

Athene's September 2026 'Asset Risk & Stress Considerations' investor-site update was referenced via a secondary source but not independently read this pass - a priority follow-up given its direct relevance to the central bear case.

APO.confidence_in_thesis: low - the core fee/AUM growth story is strong, but the confirmed liquidity-gating event and the insurance-linked earnings volatility are real, only partially quantified risks that this pass could not fully resolve

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists yet for APO (wave 6 not yet valued by the systematic model), so v1_verdict is null and there is nothing to reconcile; my own reverse-DCF sense using Adjusted Net Income (P/E ~14-15x on ANI, WACC ~10-11%) implies only ~4-6% perpetual earnings growth priced in, well below the 25% YoY FRE/AUM growth actually delivered and below my base case of 8-12% 10-year ANI/share growth, i.e. the stock looks cheap on core earnings - but this reverse-DCF does not directly price the Athene balance-sheet/duration risk or the private-credit gating event, which are the more relevant risk lenses here.

APO.scenario_basis: Starting point run-rate Adjusted Net Income/share ~$2.11 (Q2 2026) annualized to ~$8.10-8.50; base case assumes 8-12% ANI/share growth (AUM compounding off $1.05tn base, decelerating but still double-digit, plus buyback accretion) with modest multiple re-rating from ~14-15x toward ~16x as gating concerns prove contained; bear assumes the private-credit gating event spreads, FRE growth stalls to low-single-digit, and the multiple compresses toward ~10x on credit-quality fears; bull assumes gating proves a one-off, FRE/AUM growth sustains near 20%+, and the multiple re-rates toward 18-19x, closer to peer (BX/KKR) levels; dividend yield (~1.5-2%) added in all scenarios.
